TABRISI:18:10-12/r3.anchor: وقيل معناه دلنا على أمر فيه نجاتنا لأن الرشد والنجاة بمعنى

TABRISI:18:10-12/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:10-12/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:10-12/r4.claim: The youths were believers who concealed Islam from a ruler named Daqiyānūs in Ephesus; he worshiped idols and killed opponents, though another account calls him a Magian who promoted that religion.
TABRISI:18:10-12/r4.anchor: وكان اسم الملك دقيانوس واسم مدينتهم أفسوس وكان ملكهم يعبد الأصنام ويدعو إليها

TABRISI:18:10-12/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:10-12/r5.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
TABRISI:18:10-12/r5.claim: ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr says the youths were close associates of the king who hid their faith from one another until they met, disclosed it, and fled to the cave.
TABRISI:18:10-12/r5.anchor: عن عبيد بن عمير وقيل إنهم كانوا قبل بعث عيسى ع

TABRISI:18:10-12/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:10-12/r6.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:18:10-12/r6.claim: One account says they followed the religion of Jesus after the people of the Gospel had passed away; another places them before Jesus’s mission.
TABRISI:18:10-12/r6.anchor: على دين المسيح لما برح أهل الإنجيل

THALABI:v6p147/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p147/r1.speaker: ابن إسحاق
THALABI:v6p147/r1.claim: Ibn Ishaq narrates that pagan Roman ruler Decius persecuted Christians in Ephesus; eight noble youths kept monotheism, prayed and fasted, then fled the forced choice between idol worship and death after believers were tortured and displayed on the city walls.
THALABI:v6p147/r1.anchor: فقال محمد بن إسحاق بن يسار: مرج أهل الإنجيل وعظمت فيهم الخطايا وطغت فيهم الملوك

THALABI:v6p147/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p147/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p147/r2.claim: The youths' prayer declares God alone as Lord of heaven and earth and says invoking another deity would be an outrageous falsehood; they ask for the persecution to be lifted.
THALABI:v6p147/r2.anchor: ربنا رب السماوات والأرض لن ندعوا من دونه إلها لقد قلنا إذا شططا

THALABI:v6p157/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p157/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p157/r2.claim: The youths' taking refuge means going and joining the cave, a cavern in Mount Yanjalus called Khayram.
THALABI:v6p157/r2.anchor: إذ أوى أي صار وانضم الفتية إلى الكهف، وهو غار في جبل ينجلوس

THALABI:v6p157/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p157/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p157/r3.claim: Their prayer asks God to ease for them what they seek of His good pleasure.
THALABI:v6p157/r3.anchor: أي يسر لنا ما نلتمس من رضاك

THALABI:v6p157/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p157/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p157/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets right guidance as a safe way out of the cave.
THALABI:v6p157/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: رشدا أي مخرجا من الغار في سلامة

THALABI:v6p157/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p157/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p157/r5.claim: Another interpretation takes rushd to mean correctness.

THALABI:v6p204/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p204/r1.speaker: معاذ
THALABI:v6p204/r1.claim: The Prophet says reciting the beginning and end of Surat al-Kahf gives light from head to foot, while reciting all of it gives light from earth to heaven.
THALABI:v6p204/r1.anchor: من قرأ أول سورة الكهف وآخرها كانت له نورا من قرنه إلى قدمه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p537/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p537/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p537/r1.claim: The opening idh cannot attach to the preceding question because the youths' flight was long before the Prophet; it attaches to an omitted command, remember when they fled.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p537/r1.anchor: لا يجوز أن يكون متعلقا بما قبله على تقدير: أم حسبت إذ أوى الفتية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p537/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p537/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p537/r2.claim: The youths went to the cave and made it their shelter; Ibn Abbas says they fled there.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p537/r2.anchor: ومعنى {أوى الفتية إلى الكهف}: صاروا إليه وجعلوه مأواهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p537/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p537/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p537/r3.claim: He glosses their going to the cave as fleeing to it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p537/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يريد هربوا إلى الكهف)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p537/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p537/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p537/r4.claim: After fleeing those pursuing them, the youths prayed for mercy, understood here as forgiveness and provision.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p537/r4.anchor: لما هربوا عمن يطلبهم اشتغلوا بالدعاء والتضرع إلى الله تعالى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p537/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p537/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p537/r5.claim: They ask for mercy from God alone so that it will make them independent of everyone else.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p537/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يريدون تغنينا بها عن جميع من سواك)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p538/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p538/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p538/r1.claim: Hayyiʾ means set right or prepare; rushd and its related forms are the opposite of error.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p538/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p538/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p538/r2.claim: He explains the prayer as asking for guidance to what brings one near to God and pleases Him; Ibn Abbas says to direct their deeds toward God's love.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p538/r2.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: (أي أرشدنا إلى ما يقرب منك ويزلف عندك)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p538/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p538/r3.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p538/r3.claim: They parse the request as having an omitted noun, a thing of right guidance; further omission yields the sense, prepare what will enable us to attain guidance.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p538/r3.anchor: وقال أهل المعاني: (تقدير الآية: هيئ لنا من أمرنا ذا رشد)

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:10-12/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:10-12/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:10-12/r1.claim: The youths fled to the cave from their pursuers, devoted themselves to supplication, and asked for forgiveness, provision, and guidance toward what brings them near God.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:10-12/r1.anchor: الفتية إلى الكهف } هربوا إليه ممن يطلبهم

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p173/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p173/r1.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p173/r1.claim: Al-Suddī interprets the mercy the youths ask for as provision and 'from You' as from God's presence.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p173/r1.anchor: {من لدنك} [الكهف: 10] من عندك. {رحمة} [الكهف: 10] ، يعني: رزقا. وهو تفسير السدي.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p173/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p173/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p173/r2.claim: The youths were believers who fled their unbelieving people, fearing they would be killed for their faith.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p173/r2.anchor: قال: {وهيئ لنا من أمرنا رشدا} [الكهف: 10] كانوا قوما قد آمنوا، فروا بدينهم من قومهم

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:9/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:9/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:9/r1.claim: The story in 18:9–26 illustrates the coming of the Hour and resurrection, making these ideas easier for people to grasp.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:9/r1.anchor: kıyametin kopacağını ve âhirette ölülerin diriltileceğini insanların daha kolay kavrayabilmeleri için 9-26. âyetlerde ibret verici bir olaya

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:9/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:9/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:9/r2.claim: Kahf means a large, wide mountain cave; Companions of the Cave names people said to have slept there for years and then awakened.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:9/r2.anchor: Kehf “dağda bulunan büyük ve geniş mağara”; Ashâb-ı Kehf ise, “mağara arkadaşları” demek olup bir mağarada yıllarca uyutulduktan sonra tekrar uyandırıldıkları haber verilen kişiler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:9/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:9/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:9/r7.claim: Although reports connect the youths to Jesus’ religion, the Quran does not identify them and presents only selected details for instruction; the author summarizes their flight, long sleep, awakening, and the townspeople’s recognition of resurrection.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:9/r7.anchor: Kur’an-ı Kerîm, bu konuda açıklama yapmamış, ancak ibret alınması için bazı yönleriyle tasvir etmiştir. Olay kısaca şöyledir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:9/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:9/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:9/r8.claim: The Quran gives neither the event’s place and date nor the youths’ number; guesses about their number are baseless speculation, known only to God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:9/r8.anchor: Kur’an-ı Kerîm olayın nerede ve ne zaman meydana geldiğine dair bilgi vermediği gibi, bu gençlerin sayıları hakkındaki iddiaları da, “karanlığa taş atma”

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:9/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:9/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:9/r9.claim: Long-sleep-and-awakening stories also occur in Indian scriptures, the Talmud’s accounts of people sleeping 70 or 60 years, and Christianity’s Seven Sleepers of Ephesus.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:9/r9.anchor: Hint kutsal kitaplarında bir tek kişinin uzun süre uykuda kalması olayına rastlandığı gibi, yahudilerin kutsal kitabı olan Talmud’da da bir şahsın yetmiş yıl

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:9/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:9/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:9/r10.claim: Meccans questioned the Prophet after learning of the story from Jewish scholars in Medina; the story answered their test, and verse 9’s question reflects the event’s astonishing nature.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:9/r10.anchor: Medine’deki yahudi âlimlerinden Ashâb-ı Kehf hakkında bilgi alan Mekkeliler, olayı hayret verici buldular ve Hz. Peygamber’i imtihan etmek için olay hakkında ona sorular sordular.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The verb rashada means to be guided and granted steadfastness; the expression about one’s affair means guidance in that matter.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The verb رَشَدَ means that he was guided and bestowed with steadfastness

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The young believers' sense of truth made them disregard danger and expediency when the truth awakened in them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: these were young people. When the sense of honour for the truth once awakens in them

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Their prayer for guidance and perseverance was wise and apt at this precarious moment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: they supplicated before God for guidance and perseverance at this precarious instant

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: These verses summarize the whole story before its details, keeping its purpose in view so secondary details do not obscure it; the Qur'an often uses this narrative pattern.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: this verse and the next two present a summary of the whole anecdote

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Against exegetes who treat the promise of mercy and provision as the youths' own speech, Islahi says its certainty marks it as God's promise; a humble person could voice it only as prayer or yearning, as in verse 10.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: constitutes the promise of divine help cannot be stated by a humble individual

FARRA:v2p134/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p134/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p134/r5.claim: The hamza in هيئ is written on an alif here; normally a hamza is seated according to the preceding vowel, though Arabs sometimes use alif in every position.
FARRA:v2p134/r5.anchor: وقوله: هيئ [10] كتبت الهمزة بالألف (وهيأ) بهجائه. وأكثر ما يكتب الهمز على ما قبله.

FARRA:v2p134/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p134/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p134/r6.claim: The ʿAbd Allāh codex reportedly wrote شيأ and يستهزأون with alif in positions where the more common orthography uses another seat.
FARRA:v2p134/r6.anchor: قال: ورأيتها في مصحف عبد الله (شيأ) في رفعه وخفضه بالألف.

FARRA:v2p134/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p134/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p134/r7.claim: The first spelling pattern is more common in books, although the alif spelling is analogical to the word’s origin.
FARRA:v2p134/r7.anchor: فإن كان ما قبله مفتوحا كتبت بالألف. وإن كان مضموما كتب بالواو

STUDYQURAN:18:60/r60.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:60/r60.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:60/r60.claim: Khiḍr’s paired gift of mercy and knowledge echoes the youths’ prayer for mercy from God’s Presence.
STUDYQURAN:18:60/r60.anchor: echoes the supplication of the youths of the cave in v. 10, where they pray to God seeking mercy from Thy Presence

STUDYQURAN:18:60/r68.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:60/r68.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:60/r68.claim: Moses asks for sound judgment; the cave youths likewise ask God for sound judgment in their affairs.
STUDYQURAN:18:60/r68.anchor: in v. 10, the youths of the cave also pray to God to grant them sound judgment in their affairs
